$comment: Single source of truth for STL set DISTRIBUTION. Marketing copy stays in
content/pages/*.yml; this file owns only the facts that decide whether a
set can be bought and where its files come from.
Two consumers read this exact file, which is why it is JSON and why it
lives inside nuxt-site/ (the Worker bundles it at build time; there is no
filesystem on Workers at runtime):
- the Nuxt server  : imported by server/utils/sets.ts
- the publish script: scripts/publish-paid-sets.sh, via jq
Paid sets stage in paid-sets/, NOT under assets/ — that tree is served
publicly by the Nuxt site, so a paid model placed there ships to anyone.
DRIP-FEED RELEASE: `status` is the flag. 'coming-soon' renders the faction
card as it looks today and makes /api/checkout refuse the set. It never
pulls files from people who already bought them: purchases are perpetual. Flipping one set to 'available' is the entire release action
- no code change - but do it only after publish-paid-sets.sh has pushed
that set's files to R2 and priceUsd below is filled in. Checkout builds
the Stripe line item from priceUsd, so there is no Price to create.
`earlyBird` only labels the price as an early-bird price in the shop.
`version` is the R2 path segment. Bump it when you re-publish changed STLs;
old buyers keep working because entitlements are per-set, not per-version,
and the download route always resolves to the current version.
NEVER remove or rename a paid set's `id` once it has sold: purchases are
recorded against it, and a buyer's download link names it.
BUNDLES are one zip holding several sets, one folder each, with the print
guide at the top. They are not sold on their own: an order that includes
every PAID set in `includes` gets the bundle zip on its order page (free
sets in `includes` ride along). Buying all five fleets is still five
line items at the per-set price. The R2 key carries every included set's
version, so bumping any of them points the site at a zip that
`npx jake publish-sets` has to rebuild; until it does, the order page
just offers the per-set downloads.
